+import copy
+import pickle
+
+import pytest
+from lark import Token
+
+
+class TaggedToken(Token):
+    pass
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cls", [Token, TaggedToken])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("transport", [copy.deepcopy, lambda t: pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(t))])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("positions", [(7, 3, 2, 3, 6, 11), (None,) * 6])
+def test_token_transport(cls, transport, positions):
+    token = cls("NAME", "word", *positions)
+    result = transport(token)
+    assert result is not token
+    assert type(result) is cls
+    assert str(result) == str(token)
+    for field in ("type", "value", "start_pos", "line", "column", "end_line", "end_column", "end_pos"):
+        assert getattr(result, field) == getattr(token, field)
+
+
+def test_deepcopy_token_memo():
+    token = Token("NAME", "word", 7, 3, 2, 3, 6, 11)
+    result = copy.deepcopy([token, token])
+    assert result[0] is result[1]

spec.question: Make `Token` transport lossless across both `copy.deepcopy()` and a pickle round trip. Each route must produce a distinct token preserving its concrete class, type, string value, and all six position fields: `start_pos`, `line`, `column`, `end_line`, `end_column`, and `end_pos`, including fields whose value is `None`. Deep-copying a container that contains the same token twice must still preserve that sharing in the copied container. Support ordinary `Token` subclasses that inherit its constructor without adding state. Deliver a unified diff against production files only.
